subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, the Boolean State Explosion Audit, the Refactor Playbook, Philosophy, Verification, and Do NOT Use When) and standard React composition practice (compound components, context providers, explicit variants, children-over-render-props, React 19 ref-as-prop / use()).

cases.scenario: A reviewer is asked to approve a PR that adds a fifth boolean prop (isCompact) to a Card component that already has isSelected, isLoading, isError, and isClickable. The rendering logic is a chain of nested ternaries.
cases.context: The team keeps shipping new card variations by adding flags; bugs appear in flag combinations QA never tested.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to the PR?
expected_flags: Run the boolean state-explosion audit: 5 booleans -> 32 combinations, most impossible/untested
Treat the API as broken at 3+ booleans until the audit proves otherwise
Recommend enumerating valid states and naming them as explicit variant components
Flag the nested-ternary rendering chain as the symptom of the flag explosion
expected_fix_hints: Inventory flags, delete impossible states, extract explicit variants
Add one example or test per valid variant
absent_signals: Do not approve adding the fifth boolean as-is
Do not solve it by adding more conditional branches

cases.scenario: A team is building a Tabs component and the proposed API is <Tabs tabs={[{label, content}]} activeIndex={i} onChange={fn} renderTab={fn} renderPanel={fn} />.
cases.context: Consumers need to customize individual tab and panel markup and keep the active tab in sync.
cases.question: What component API should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: Recommend a compound component: Tabs.List, Tabs.Tab, Tabs.Panel sharing state through a context provider
Lift active-tab state into the provider so siblings stay in sync without prop drilling
Replace renderTab/renderPanel render props with children composition
Provider owns state, actions, and meta; consumers compose around the contract
expected_fix_hints: Expose Tabs.* compound children backed by a context provider
Pass markup as children rather than renderX callbacks
absent_signals: Do not keep the flat data-array + render-prop API
Do not drill activeIndex/onChange through every level

cases.scenario: A Modal component takes renderHeader, renderBody, and renderFooter props, each a function returning JSX. New consumers find the API awkward and keep passing inline arrow functions.
cases.context: The slots are structurally static — header/body/footer always render in the same positions.
cases.question: How should the agent improve the Modal API?
expected_flags: Replace the renderHeader/renderBody/renderFooter render props with children composition
Expose compound slots (e.g. Modal.Header, Modal.Body, Modal.Footer) or accept structured children
Children-over-render-props: use children for composition rather than renderX callbacks
Notes render props add ceremony where static structural slots only need children
expected_fix_hints: Convert renderX props into composable children / compound slots
Keep render props only where a child genuinely needs provider-derived values
absent_signals: Do not keep three renderX function props for static slots

cases.scenario: A filter sidebar and a results grid are siblings that both need the current filter state. The current code threads filters and setFilters down through four intermediate components as props.
cases.context: Adding a new filter means editing every intermediate component's prop signature.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the state?
expected_flags: Lift the filter state into a context provider that both siblings consume
Provider exposes state, actions, and meta; consumers read the contract directly
Eliminates prop drilling through intermediate components
Decouples consumers from how the filter state is managed
expected_fix_hints: Have sidebar and grid read from context instead of threaded props
absent_signals: Do not keep drilling filters/setFilters through intermediaries
Do not duplicate filter state in both siblings

cases.scenario: A component library targeting React 19 still wraps every component in forwardRef and reads context with useContext() throughout.
cases.context: The team has upgraded to React 19 and wants to adopt the current API surface.
cases.question: What React 19 changes should the agent apply?
expected_flags: Drop forwardRef — pass ref as a regular prop in React 19
Use use() instead of useContext() to read context
Notes this section applies to React 19+ only (skip on React 18 or earlier)
Migration is API-shape modernization, not behavior change
expected_fix_hints: Remove forwardRef wrappers; accept ref as a normal prop
absent_signals: Do not apply React 19 changes to a stated React 18 codebase
Do not keep forwardRef solely out of habit on React 19

cases.scenario: An engineer proposes wrapping a single leaf component that has one boolean (isOpen) used only by itself in a full context provider with state/actions/meta 'to follow the composition pattern.'
cases.context: The component has no siblings needing the state and no flag explosion.
cases.question: How should the agent respond?
expected_flags: A single self-contained boolean with no shared-state need does not warrant a provider
Lift state into a provider only when siblings need it or a flag explosion exists
The audit (count reachable states) shows no explosion here — local state is fine
Applying the heaviest pattern by default is over-engineering, not the discipline
expected_fix_hints: Keep isOpen as local component state
Reserve the provider pattern for shared state or audited flag explosions
absent_signals: Do not introduce a context provider for purely local single-flag state
Do not treat 'use composition' as 'always add a provider'
